title: Screens
hookLine: what you give attention to becomes your life
tomorrow: a burned-out prophet asks to die. what does God give him first?

lines: TAKEN A FEW SECONDS AT A TIME.
cards: One tap to check the essay prompt. Then a video, a reply, a video about the reply, and the clock says 1:40. Nobody decided to spend those hours; they were taken a few seconds at a time.

Proverbs knew nothing about phones, but it knew where a life gets steered from: “Keep thy heart with all diligence; for out of it are the issues of life.” What gets your attention, little by little, becomes the life.

teach.h: THE EYE IS THE LIGHT OF THE BODY.
teach.b: Jesus says something close about the eyes: “The light of the body is the eye: if therefore thine eye be single, thy whole body shall be full of light.”
Single: one focus, not scattered in a hundred directions. Whatever the eye keeps returning to, the rest of a person slowly fills with. That's today's idea in an old room.
A psalm turns it into a request: “Turn away mine eyes from beholding vanity; and quicken thou me in thy way.” Vanity here means emptiness, things with nothing inside. Quicken means bring to life.

And Paul gives the Philippians a list to aim at: “whatsoever things are true, whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just, whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely”, and then, “think on these things.”
Notice the list doesn't ban anything. A screen can carry a friend's face, a psalm read aloud, a sermon, a recipe for someone who's sick. The question isn't the glass.
Guarding attention isn't being afraid of the phone. It's choosing, before the evening starts, what gets your eyes, because the evening will choose otherwise.

how: Some Christians keep a screen-free evening or day each week, or set aside social media during Lent; others put phones away during prayer, worship and meals.

o: a modern sin the Bible warns against by name
windows that can carry anything to your eyes
tools so neutral they change nothing at all

games.q: where the eye goes — tap the pairs.
p: out of it are the issues of life

s: Philippians gives a list of things to think on
whatsoever things are true, honest, just, pure, lovely: think on these things.
the Bible teaches that screens and technology are sinful
it never mentions them; it asks what the eye keeps returning to.
in Matthew, the eye has little to do with the rest of the body
the light of the body is the eye: a single eye fills the whole body with light.

games.q: it's 9 p.m. on your planned screen-free evening, and a friend sends a link: "you HAVE to see this." what fits a single eye?
o: reply "tomorrow" and leave the phone where it is.
watch it quickly so you don't fall behind the joke.
delete every app tonight; screens are the enemy.
games.why: the list in Philippians doesn't ban screens; it aims the eye. one focus tonight, and the link will still be there tomorrow.

practice: Put your phone face down, in another room if you can. Sit with your hands open and empty on your knees, and let them stay empty for the whole sit; notice each time they reach for something to hold.
If you pray, you can borrow the psalm's words: turn away mine eyes from beholding vanity.

wordCard.voice: Screens. Windows that can carry anything to the eye; the eye still decides what fills the body.

orig.note: Greek: single, simple, undivided. the eye in Matthew 6:22.

carryVoice: Your line: guard your attention, because whatever gets it slowly becomes your life. Take care.
